message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that’s carried out only a few times a decade.  In practice, the whole process—from stripping old paint to applying fresh layers—takes roughly **two months**.

Here’s why:

| Factor | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Height** | 330 m (1,083 ft) |
| **Surface area** | ~10 000 m² (about 107 000 ft²) |
| **Rivets** | 18 038 |
| **Paint used** | ~60 tons (≈ 27 000 kg) |
| **Frequency** | Every 7–8 years (to prevent rust) |

During the two‑month window, workers use scaffolding, cranes, and specialized equipment to reach all parts of the structure. They first strip old paint, treat rusted areas, then apply multiple coats of protective paint. The schedule is tightly coordinated to minimize disruption to visitors and to ensure the tower remains safe and visually striking.
